slides.title: Consumer Marketing
slides.text:
Consumer Marketing
Meaning : It consists of all activities involved in marketing of products and services to individuals and households that buy goods and services for personal consumption.
Features: 1. Large number of buyers 2. Smaller purchase quantities 3. Direct demand 4. Shorter buying process

slides.text:
Industrial Marketing
• Meaning: It consists of all activities involved in the marketing of product and services to
organizations that use those products and services in the production of consumer or
industrial products and services, and to facilitate the operation of their enterprises.
• Features:
1. Fewer, but larger market
2. Close relationship between seller and buyer
3. Complex buying process due to approval from different authorities
4. Derived demand

slides.title: Consumer Vs Industrial marketing
slides.text:
Consumer Vs Industrial marketing
Products are standardized and can be mass marketed
Consumer goods and services are purchased for personal consumption
Market structure is geographically dispersed
Demand for consumer goods and services is direct demand
Emphasis on advertising for promotion
Products are niche specific
Industrial goods and services are purchased for production of other goods and services
Market structure is geographically concentrated.
Demand for industrial goods and services is derived demand
Emphasis on personal selling for promotion

Needs, Wants and Demands
• Needs:
Needs are the basic human requirements like food, security, clothing,
and survival.
• Wants:
Wants are the form taken by needs as they are shaped by culture and
individual personality
.
• Demands:
When backed by an ability to pay, that is, buying power - wants
become demands

slides.text:
Products and Services
• Products- A product is anything that can be offered to a market to satisfy a
need or want
• Goods- Any tangible item that can offered to satisfy a need or want
• Services- Any activity or benefit that one party can offer to another which is
essentially intangible and does not result in ownership of anything.
Examples are banking, airline, hotel and household appliance repair services.

slides.text:
Production Concept
• This concept focuses on the internal capabilities of the firm rather than on desires and needs of the
marketplace.
• Marketing strategy: Production efficiency.
• works on an assumption that consumers prefer a product which is inexpensive and widely available.
• Holds in following situations:
1. Demand exceeds Supply
2. Product cost is too high
Pros:
1. Economies of Scale
2. Decreased Production cost
Cons:
1. No focus on Product quality
2. Does not consider needs of the marketplace

slides.text:
Product Concept
• This concept holds that consumers will favour products that offer the most in quality,
performance and features.
• Marketing strategy : Continuous product improvements.
• Pros:
1. Improved product quality
• Cons:
1. Fail to appeal to customers whose demands are driven by other factors like price, availability,
usability, etc.
2. Leads to marketing myopia, focusing on fulfillment of immediate needs of the company.

slides.text:
Selling Concept
• This concept is based on the idea that people will buy more goods and services if aggressive
sales techniques are used.
• Main focus is to make money.
• Marketing strategy: Aggressive Selling of products that firms make.
• Pros:
1. High sales of products especially unsought products
• Cons:
1. Lack of understanding of marketplace needs and wants
2. doesn’t include building relations with customers. Hence repeated sales are very less.

Focus on creating value for customers

Pros: 1. Firms establishes a relationship with the customer and generate profits in the long run. 2. Deliver superior customer value
